**(a) Linearized-wave datum.** Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be a
nonempty open set and let $K\subseteq\Omega$ be a nonempty compact set. Fix a
length scale $L>0$, and use the numerical threshold $\delta_0=1/16$ and
chart control functional $B_K$ defined in
[[pthm-gr-linearized-field-equations]] clause (d) for this $K,L$. A
**linearized-wave datum on $K$** consists of:

- a flat linearized family $(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ over $\Omega$ with
  perturbation $h$ ([[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]]) such that
  $B_K(h)<\infty$ in the chart control functional of that clause;
- the real cosmological parameter $\Lambda$ and a smooth family
  $\mathcal T(\lambda)$ of stress-energy tensor fields on $\Omega$ for
  $\lambda\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$, with component fields smooth
  jointly in $(\lambda,x)$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]);
- the zeroth-order compatibility condition
  $\kappa\mathcal T_{ab}(0)=\Lambda\eta_{ab}$, where
  $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$; define the linearized source field, with curvature
  units, by $S_{ab}:=\kappa\,\partial_\lambda\mathcal T_{ab}(\lambda)|_0$,
  and require
  $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)+\Lambda h_{ab}=S_{ab}$ in the sense of
  [[def-gr-plane-wave-perturbation]] clause (e);
- a nonzero real amplitude $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ for
  which $g(\lambda):=\eta+\lambda h$ is a Lorentzian metric of signature
  $(-,+,+,+)$ on a neighborhood of $K$.

The parameter $\lambda$ is dimensionless, and in the adopted SI length
coordinates $S_{ab}$, $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)$ and $\Lambda h_{ab}$ have units
$\mathrm m^{-2}$, whereas $\mathcal T_{ab}$ has energy-density units and
$\kappa\mathcal T_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm m^{-2}$
([[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]). The $B_K$ and $\delta_0$
values in the chart Taylor estimate are numerical controls: evaluate
component functions and their coordinate derivatives as SI numerical values
in this fixed length-coordinate chart, then form the displayed real-valued
functional. It is not a physical observable or an intrinsic norm. In this
fixed numerical convention, $B_K$, $\delta_0$ and $C_{K,L}$ are real control
numbers and $C_{K,L}B_K^2/L^2$ has the residual component unit
$\mathrm m^{-2}$ for $L$ in metres. The datum is a
**linearized vacuum wave datum** when $S=0$ and $\Lambda=0$. If in addition
the perturbation is a TT planar perturbation with amplitudes $A_+,A_\times$
([[def-gr-plane-wave-perturbation]] clause (b)), the datum is a **TT
linearized-wave datum**. Its **approximation defect** is

where $G$ is the Einstein tensor of the exact metric $\eta+\lambda h$;
this is the residual against the specified exact stress-energy family, not
against its first-order coefficient alone. In length coordinates it has
units $\mathrm m^{-2}$. The datum is **within the quadratic approximation**
when $|\lambda|B_K(h)\le\delta_0$. This uses the chosen threshold rather than
an unspecified existential $\delta_0/B_K(h)$, and also covers $B_K(h)=0$.
Whether a datum satisfies any of these conditions is a property of the
given data; this definition names the data, the condition and the defect and
asserts neither existence nor a bound.

- **Why the regime conditions are separate from the detector.** Clause (a)
  packages the approximation hypotheses — a linearized family, a length
  scale, a source and parameter, a compact set and an amplitude — so that
  later theorems can quantify the approximation defect and the response
  without repeating them. When $\Lambda=0$ and the specified family satisfies
  $\mathcal T(\lambda)=0$ identically, the quadratic residual bound is the
  content of [[pthm-gr-linearized-field-equations]] clause (d) and
  [[thm-gr-tt-plane-wave-solutions]] clause (c). Merely having $S=0$ allows
  higher-order terms in $\mathcal T(\lambda)$, for which no residual bound is
  asserted here; the definition itself only names the defect.

- a *worldline entry*: a $C^1$ future timelike worldline $h:I\to M$ on an
  interval $I$ with nonempty interior, parametrized by proper time, so that its
  four-velocity $U:=h'$ satisfies $g(U,U)=-c^2$
  ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]],
  [[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]), or the
  restriction of such a worldline to a subinterval;
- an *observer entry*: an observer at a point, that is a future unit timelike
  vector $n$ with $g(n,n)=-1$, or a smooth observer congruence
  ([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]],
  [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]);
- a *ray entry*: a smooth curve $\eta:J\to M$, where $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ is
  an interval with nonempty interior, that is a future-directed null geodesic
  of $\nabla$; thus it is affinely parametrized and satisfies
  $\nabla_{\eta'}\eta'=0$, $g(\eta',\eta')=0$ and $\eta'$ is future-directed,
  with the one-sided convention at included endpoints
  ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
  [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
  [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] clause (iii));
- a *chart entry*: a smooth chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]);
- an *azimuth entry*: a continuous real function $\varphi:K\to\mathbb R$
  on a compact parameter interval $K=[t_1,t_2]$ of a worldline entry, with
  values in radians, together with the local azimuth chart designations and
  compatibility conditions specified in (b)4; this is supplied data, not an
  assertion that such a function exists;
- a *detector entry*: the data of the ideal two-body detector of the
  linearized-wave regime, namely a TT linearized-wave datum, a reference point
  $x_0$, a separation vector $\delta\ne0$ with $\delta^0=0$, the arm direction
  $e_\delta$, and a parameter value $s$, as in
  [[def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling]] clauses (a)-(c);
- a *parameter entry*: a finite tuple of real numbers in a declared subset of
  $\mathbb R^m$, each component with declared units;
- an *annotation entry*: a finite string recording declared conditions of the
  configuration and, where a datum is taken from a report, the bibliographic
  identification of that report.

[L4] The first-order formulas are linear in $h$ and give $\bar h_{00}=-4\varphi$, $\bar h_{0i}=\bar h_{ij}=0$ and $G^{(1)}_{ab}=-\frac12\Box\bar h_{ab}+\partial^c\partial_{(a}\bar h_{b)c}-\frac12\eta_{ab}\partial^c\partial^d\bar h_{cd}$; for stationary fields $\Box=\Delta$ ([[thm-gr-flat-linearized-curvature-and-gauge]] clause (c), [[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]] clauses (a) and (c)).

**(d) Quadratic residual of a linearized vacuum wave.** Let
$K\subseteq\Omega$ be a nonempty compact set and let $L>0$ be a length scale. In the fixed
SI numerical chart define the real control functional
$$B_K(A):=\sup_K\max_{a,b}|A_{ab}|+L^{-1}\sup_K\max_{a,b,c}|\partial_cA_{ab}|+L^{-2}\sup_K\max_{a,b,c,d}|\partial_c\partial_dA_{ab}|.$$

Take the fixed dimensionless numerical threshold $\delta_0:=1/16$. If $h$ is
a smooth symmetric perturbation on a neighborhood of $K$ with
$G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$ on $K$, then there is a finite dimensionless numerical
constant $C_{K,L}$ such that, for every real $\lambda$ with
$|\lambda|B_K(h)\le\delta_0$,
$$\bigl|G_{ab}(\eta+\lambda h)(p)\bigr|\le C_{K,L}\,\lambda^2B_K(h)^2/L^2\qquad(p\in K).$$

The functional $B_K$ and threshold are numerical chart controls, not physical
observables; each component and derivative is first evaluated in the fixed
SI length-coordinate convention. With $L$ in metres, the displayed residual
has units $\mathrm m^{-2}$. For the zero-source branch $T(\lambda)=0$ with
$\Lambda=0$, this bounds the residual of the exact vacuum field law on $K$.

**Given:** The adopted postulates, a flat linearized family $(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ over $\Omega$, a smooth family $T(\lambda)$ of symmetric fields satisfying the field law for every $\lambda$, and a nonempty compact set $K\subseteq\Omega$ with $L>0$; for clause (e), also assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

[L2] In harmonic gauge $\partial^a\bar h_{ab}=0$ one has $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=-\tfrac12\Box\bar h_{ab}$, and $G^{(1)}$ is unchanged under $h\mapsto h-\partial\xi-\partial\xi$ ([[thm-gr-flat-linearized-curvature-and-gauge]] clauses (c)-(e), [[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]] clauses (c)-(d)). For the all-space existence assertion, the nonnegative-radius spherical-mean kernel and zero-data Duhamel construction are those of [[thm-gr-flat-wave-equation-duhamel-and-harmonic-gauge]] clauses (a)-(b); $H_f(x,0)=0$ and its right derivative at $s=0$ is $f(x)$. The signed extension used for negative time differences is smooth as shown in proof step 4.1 below, where [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]] and [[thm-linear-change-of-variables-for-lebesgue-measure]] justify antipodal symmetry and hence preserves these initial data.

[L3] In the inertial chart the Einstein tensor of $\eta+A$ is a smooth function of the finite component list $(A_{ab},\partial_cA_{ab},\partial_c\partial_dA_{ab})$ whenever $\eta+A$ is nondegenerate; at the zero list it vanishes, and its derivative there is $G^{(1)}(A)$, which is linear in $A$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]], [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]], [[thm-gr-flat-linearized-curvature-and-gauge]] clauses (a), (e), [[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]] clause (b)). The Taylor estimate of [[cor-taylor-lagrange-and-cauchy-remainders]] applies on compact subsets of this finite-dimensional jet domain, and matrices within maximum-entry distance $1/8$ of $\eta$ are Lorentzian ([[lem-gr-lorentzian-perturbations-remain-lorentzian]] clause (a)).

1.1 (The residual family.) Define $\Phi_{ab}(\lambda,p):=G_{ab}(g(\lambda))(p)+\Lambda g_{ab}(\lambda)(p)-\kappa T_{ab}(\lambda,p)$ for $(\lambda,p)\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)\times\Omega$. By [L1] and the smoothness of $T$, each component $\Phi_{ab}$ is differentiable in $\lambda$ at every $\lambda$. By hypothesis $\Phi_{ab}(\lambda,p)=0$ for all $(\lambda,p)$, so $\partial_\lambda\Phi_{ab}(0,p)=0$ for every $p$ (the difference quotients of the identically zero function vanish). [A1, L1, given]

1.3 (Quadratic residual.) Let $h$ satisfy $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$ on $K$ and choose $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ with $|\lambda|B_K(h)\le\delta_0=1/16$. Put $A:=\lambda h$ and at each $p\in K$ let $V_A(p)$ be the finite list $(A_{ab},\partial_cA_{ab},\partial_c\partial_dA_{ab})$. By the displayed definition of $B_K$, $\|V_A(p)\|_{\max}\le m_LB_K(A)$, where $m_L:=\max\{1,L,L^2\}$; in particular $|A_{ab}(p)|\le1/16<1/8$, so [L3] makes $\eta+A$ Lorentzian. The jet lists along all segments $tV_A(p)$, $p\in K$, $0\le t\le1$, lie in the compact set given by $\max|A_{ab}|\le1/16$, $\max|\partial_cA_{ab}|\le L\delta_0$ and $\max|\partial_c\partial_dA_{ab}|\le L^2\delta_0$. On this set the smooth Einstein-tensor map of [L3] has Hessian bounded by a finite $H_{K,L}$. Taylor's estimate along $tV_A(p)$ gives $|G_{ab}(\eta+A)(p)-G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)(p)|\le\tfrac12H_{K,L}m_L^2B_K(A)^2=C_{K,L}B_K(A)^2/L^2$, with $C_{K,L}:=\tfrac12H_{K,L}m_L^2L^2$. Since $B_K(A)=|\lambda|B_K(h)$ and $G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)=\lambda G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$, this is (d). [L3, algebra]

4.1 (All-space harmonic gauge.) Let $\Omega=\mathbb R^4$, let $h$ solve the linearized vacuum equations with $\Lambda=0$, and set $F_b(x,t):=-\partial^a\bar h_{ab}(x,t)$ in the coordinates $x^0=ct$. For $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ define the signed-radius mean $\widetilde M_rf(x):=(4\pi)^{-1}\int_{S^2}f(x+r\omega)\,d\sigma(\omega)$ for $r\in\mathbb R$. The integral is smooth in $(x,r)$ by differentiation under the integral on compact parameter sets, as in the proof of [[thm-gr-flat-wave-equation-duhamel-and-harmonic-gauge]] clause (a). The antipodal substitution $\omega\mapsto-\omega$ preserves $\sigma$: by the cone-volume definition in [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], the cone of $-E$ is the image of the cone of $E$ under $y\mapsto-y$, a linear map with determinant $-1$ in $\mathbb R^3$ and hence preserves Lebesgue measure by [[thm-linear-change-of-variables-for-lebesgue-measure]]. Thus $\widetilde M_{-r}f=\widetilde M_rf$, and for $r\ge0$ it agrees with $M_rf$. The kernel $\widetilde H_f(x,s):=s\widetilde M_{cs}f(x)$ is therefore smooth for signed $s$, odd in $s$, agrees with the kernel of [L2] for $s\ge0$, and satisfies $(c^{-2}\partial_s^2-\Delta_x)\widetilde H_f=0$: for $s>0$ this follows from [[thm-gr-flat-wave-equation-duhamel-and-harmonic-gauge]] clause (a), for $s<0$ by oddness, and at $s=0$ by smoothness and continuity. The same moving-endpoint differentiation as in that theorem's proof (b), now with this smooth two-sided kernel, shows that $\xi_b(x,t):=c^2\int_0^t\widetilde H_{F_b(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$ is smooth on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ and satisfies $(c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta_x)\xi_b=F_b$ for every signed $t$; hence $-\Box\xi_b=F_b=-\partial^a\bar h_{ab}$ and $\Box\xi_b=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}$. The gauge identity of [L2] then gives $\partial^a\bar h'_{ab}=0$ for $h'_{ab}=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a$. By gauge invariance in [L2] and the vacuum conclusion of step 3.1 applied only to $h$, $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$; applying the harmonic-gauge identity of [L2] to $h'$ yields $\Box\bar h'_{ab}=0$. This proves (e). [given, L2, step 3.1, algebra]

## Facts & Assumptions

[L4] The Christoffel family has the expansion $\Gamma^\mu{}_{ab}(\lambda,p)=\lambda\Gamma^{(1)\mu}{}_{ab}(p)+O(\lambda^2)$ with the first-order coefficient $\Gamma^{(1)\mu}{}_{ab}=\tfrac12\eta^{\mu\rho}(\partial_ah_{\rho b}+\partial_bh_{\rho a}-\partial_\rho h_{ab})$ and a quadratic remainder bounded on compact parameter sets by a Lagrange estimate; $\Gamma(0)=0$ ([[thm-gr-flat-linearized-curvature-and-gauge]] clauses (a), (e), [[cor-taylor-lagrange-and-cauchy-remainders]], [[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]] clauses (b)-(c)). Also, on a compact parameter segment and a compact set of the curves, $Q^\mu{}_a(\lambda,p):=\partial_0\Gamma^\mu{}_{0a}(\lambda,p)$ is smooth in $(\lambda,p)$, satisfies $Q(0,p)=0$ and $\partial_\lambda Q(0,p)=\partial_0\Gamma^{(1)\mu}{}_{0a}(p)$; applying Taylor's estimate to $Q$ itself gives $\partial_0\Gamma=\lambda\partial_0\Gamma^{(1)}+O(\lambda^2)$ uniformly there. Smoothness follows from the explicit metric formula, matrix inversion on the Lorentzian domain and smoothness of the profiles ([[thm-gr-flat-linearized-curvature-and-gauge]] clauses (a), (e), [[cor-taylor-lagrange-and-cauchy-remainders]]).

[L5] A continuous real function on a nonempty compact set is bounded: its relatively open sublevel sets $\{|f|<m\}$, for positive integers $m$, cover the set and have a finite subcover ([[def-compact-space]]). For $|x|\le\tfrac12$, put $r=\sqrt{1+x}>0$. Since $(r-1)(r+1)=x$, one has $r-1-x/2=-x^2/(2(r+1)^2)$, hence $|\sqrt{1+x}-1-x/2|\le x^2/2$. Squares are nonnegative, and $2|ab|\le a^2+b^2$ follows from $(|a|-|b|)^2\ge0$ ([[lem-of-square-positive]], [[def-real-order]], [[def-rational-power]]).

1.1 (Smooth signed-radius means and derivatives under the integral.) For fixed $x,r$ the integration is over the finite-measure space $(S^2,\sigma)$ with $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$; for $(x,r)$ in a compact set the integrand $\omega\mapsto f(x+r\omega)$ and each of its derivatives in $(x,r)$ is continuous on the compact set $S^2\times K$ and hence bounded, so [F3] applies on every compact parameter neighborhood and shows that $Mf$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, with $\partial_x^\alpha M_rf=M_r(\partial^\alpha f)$ and all $r$-derivatives obtained by differentiating under the integral. By [F5], changing variables $\omega\mapsto-\omega$ gives $M_{-r}f=M_rf$, and [F1]'s normalization gives $M_0f=f$. Since $(x,s)\mapsto(x,cs)$ and $s\mapsto s$ are smooth, $H_f$ is smooth, $H_f(x,0)=0$ and $\partial_sH_f(x,0)=f(x)$. [F1, F3, F5, given, algebra]

5.1 (Duhamel solution.) Define $G(x,t,v):=H_{F(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)$. From the defining integral, [step 1.1, step 4.1, F3, given, algebra]
$$G(x,t,v)=\frac{t-v}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}F\bigl(x+c(t-v)\omega,v\bigr)\,d\sigma(\omega).$$
The integrand is jointly smooth in $(x,t,v,\omega)$; on each compact parameter set every derivative is bounded on the compact sphere, so differentiation under the integral shows that $G$ is smooth. Applying the moving-endpoint rule of [F3] and the differentiation theorem of [F3] on compact parameter sets gives $u\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times I)$ with $$\partial_tu=c^2H_{F(\cdot,t)}(x,0)+c^2\int_{t_0}^t\partial_tG\,dv=c^2\int_{t_0}^t(\partial_sH_{F(\cdot,v)})(x,t-v)\,dv,$$ because $H_{g}(x,0)=0$ for every $g$ by step 1.1. Differentiating once more, the endpoint term is $c^2(\partial_sH_{F(\cdot,t)})(x,0)=c^2F(x,t)$ and the integral term is $c^2\int_{t_0}^tc^2\Delta_xH_{F(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$ by step 4.1, so $\partial_t^2u=c^2F+c^2\Delta_xu$, that is, $(c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta_x)u=F$. Also $u(x,t_0)=0$ and $\partial_tu(x,t_0)=0$ because the integration interval is a point. For compact $K\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ and $[a,b]\subseteq I$, put $v_-:=\min\{a,t_0\}$ and $v_+:=\max\{b,t_0\}$. Every oriented integration interval from $t_0$ to $t\in[a,b]$ lies in $[v_-,v_+]$, and the derivatives of $G$ are continuous on the compact set $K\times[a,b]\times[v_-,v_+]$, hence bounded there, and every derivative of $u$ on $K\times[a,b]$ is a finite sum of $v$-integrals of such derivatives together with endpoint terms, so it is bounded. No boundedness on all of $\mathbb R^3$ is claimed, since $F$ is an arbitrary smooth source. This proves (b). [step 1.1, step 4.1, F3, given, algebra]

The formula is the standard retarded solution with zero incoming data on the slab.
- **No decay hypothesis.** Every value and derivative of $u$ at a point samples only a compact sphere and a finite time interval, so no spatial decay, compact support or finite-energy assumption is used; the price is that the estimates are only local in space.

3.1 (Quadratic residual.) Fix the nonempty compact $K$ and $L>0$. Let $b_j$ be the supremum over $K$ of the maximum absolute value of the order-$j$ component derivatives of $h$, for $j=0,1,2$; these numbers are finite by [F4]. The quantity in clause (c) is $M_K=b_0+L^{-1}b_1+L^{-2}b_2$, while the supplier's control is $B_K(h)=b_0+Lb_1+L^2b_2$. Set $q_L:=\max\{1,L^2,L^4\}$. Termwise comparison gives $B_K(h)\le q_LM_K$ for every $L>0$. Take $\delta_0,C$ from [F5] for this nonempty $K$ and $L$, and choose $\lambda_0>0$ with $\lambda_0B_K(h)\le\delta_0$ and, when $M>0$, $\lambda_0<1/(2M)$; if $B_K(h)=0$, its constraint is automatic. For $|\lambda|\le\lambda_0$, put $A=\lambda h$, so $B_K(A)=|\lambda|B_K(h)\le\delta_0$. The metric is Lorentzian on all of $\mathbb R^4$ by step 1.1. Applying the residual estimate of [F5] on $K$ gives $|G_{ab}(\eta+\lambda h)(p)-G^{(1)}_{ab}(\lambda h)(p)|\le C\lambda^2B_K(h)^2/L^2\le Cq_L^2\lambda^2M_K^2/L^2$. By linearity and step 2.1, $G^{(1)}_{ab}(\lambda h)=\lambda G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$. Thus clause (c) holds with $C_K:=Cq_L^2<\infty$, also when $M_K=0$. [F4, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]
